newsitem.title: USA: US money managers less bullish on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers less bullish on US debt - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers pulled back from their bullish sentiment on U.S. debt over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Buyside managers are cooling on the market and having trouble finding value," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark fell to a modest 105.7 percent in the week ended September 30 from 105.8 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 29 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 23 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 16 percent, up from 12 percent in the week ended September 23.
Fifty-five percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 65 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 2.80 percent, against 2.66 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 18 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 19 percent in the previous week, while 27 percent underweighted it. The remaining 55 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 41 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 20 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
